chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I saw Mismāʿ in al-Madinah, and he had carried wealth to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that year, but Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام returned it. So I said to him, “Why did Abū ʿAbdillāh return to you the wealth that you carried to him?” He said: He said to me, “I said to him when I carried the wealth to him: I had been appointed over pearl-diving in al-Baḥrayn, and I obtained four hundred thousand dirhams. I have come to you with its khums, eighty thousand dirhams, and I disliked withholding it from you or exposing it [to loss], while it is your right which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has placed in our wealth.”

So he said: “Is there for us, from the land and what Allah brings forth from it, only the khums? O Abū Sayyār, surely all the earth belongs to us, so whatever Allah brings forth from it of anything, it is ours.” I said to him, “Then I should carry all of the wealth to you?” He said: “O Abū Sayyār, we have made it wholesome for you and permitted you regarding it. So keep your wealth with you. And everything of the land that is in the hands of our Shiʿah is lawful for them until our Qāʾim rises.”

Then he will collect from them the levy of what was in their hands, and he will leave the land in their hands. But as for what is in the hands of others, their earnings from the land are haram for them until our Qāʾim rises, whereupon he will take the land from their hands and expel them in humiliation.

ʿUmar ibn Yazid said: Then Abū Sayyār said to me, “I do not regard anyone among the owners of estates, nor those who administer official functions, as consuming what is halal besides me, except one for whom they have made that lawful.”

key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the land or earth, described here as belonging entirely to them
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth due mentioned here in relation to wealth and rights
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: forbidden or unlawful, describing the earnings of others from the land
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: our Shiʿah, those granted permissibility regarding land in their possession
key_terms.طَيَّبْنَاهُ: we have made it wholesome or lawful for you
key_terms.قَائِمُنَا: our Qāʾim, whose rise is linked to future enforcement
key_terms.مُحَلَّلُونَ: rendered lawful or permitted with respect to that possession

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in al-Kafi say about khums, ownership of the earth, and the Shiʿah’s use of land until the rise of the Qāʾim عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imam عليه السلام declared the earth and what it produces to belong to them, and that he permitted his Shiʿah to benefit from what is in their possession until the قيام of the Qāʾim عليه السلام. It also presents a ruling concerning permissibility, khums, and the differing status of land held by the Shiʿah and others.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I saw Misma’a at Al-Medina and he had carried some wealth to Abu Abdullahasws at that time, but Abu Abdullahasws returned it. So I said to him, ‘Abu Abdullahasws returned the wealth upon you which you had carried it to himasws’. So he said to me, ‘I said to himasws when I carried the wealth over to himasws, ‘I was in charge of the pearls of Bahrain and I attained a profit of four hundred thousand Dirhams, and I have come to youasws with its fifth (Khums), with eighty thousand Dirhams, and I disliked it that I should withhold it and turn away with It, and it is yourasws right which Allahazwj Blessed and High Made it to be in our wealth’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or what is for us<sup>asws</sup> from the earth and what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Brings out from it except the Khums, O Abu Sayyar? Surely the earth, all of it, is for us<sup>asws</sup>. So whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Brings forth from it, from anything, so it is for us<sup>asws</sup>’. So I said to him, ‘And I shall carry all of the wealth to you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Sayyar! We<sup>asws</sup> have cleaned it for you and permited you from it. So keep your wealth with you and everything what is in the hands of our<sup>asws</sup> Shias from the earth, so they are in permissibility with regards to it until our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup> rises.

So he<sup>asws</sup> would collect their levy on whatever would be in their hands and he<sup>asws</sup> would leave the land to be in their hands. And as for whatever would be in the hands of others (non-Shias), so their earning from the land is Prohibited upon them until our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup> rises. So he<sup>asws</sup> would seize the land from their hands and throw them out belittled’.

Umar Bin Yazeed said, ‘So Abu Sayyar said to him, I do not  find anyone doing business or people as in charge persons of certain tasks, who earn their living lawfully except myself and those for whom they<sup>asws</sup> ('A'immah) have made it lawful.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following.

“I saw Masma‘ in Madina. In that year he had tried to deliver a certain amount of property to abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) that he returned to him. I asked him about the reason for the return.. The narrator has said that he said to me, “When I took the property to him I said, ‘ I had become the in charge of the pearls in Bahrayn and I have made four hundred thousand Dirham profit. I have brought eighty thousand Dinar as your share. I did not like to keep your share and disregard what Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has decreed to be for you in our properties.”

Is there no more from earth and what Allah takes out of it besides one fifth for us, O abu Sayyar?” The whole earth belongs to us. Whatever Allah causes to come out therefrom it belongs to us.” I then said, “I will bring all the property to you.” He said, “O abu Sayyar, we have made it a gift for you and made it lawful for you. Take your property with you. Whatever land is in the hands of our Shi‘a it is lawful for them until Al-Qa’im will rise with Divine Authority.

He will make an agreement with them about whatever land is in their hands and will give them permission to use. Whatever land is in the hands of others their earning from it is not lawful until Al-Qa’im will rise with Divine Authority. He will take such lands away from them and will remove them humiliate

‘Umar ibn Yazid has said, “Abu Sayyar said to me, ‘ I do not find anyone doing business oor those in charge of certain tasks who would earn their living lawfully except my self and those for whom they have made it lawful.”
